## OWNER CONTINUATION (relayed from coordinating chat) — authorize a GitHub-hosted PG17 evidence run, NOT migration execution — 2026-10-18

**Owner instruction:** “Issue #74: Run the disposable PostgreSQL 17 security tests on a GitHub Actions runner instead of relying on your local Docker Desktop … PR #68: Continue withholding migration approval until … actual test evidence. lets do these.”

This comment is a **coordinator-relayed, narrow owner task instruction**; not independently authenticated as an owner-authored GitHub approval. It **authorizes preparation of the bounded GitHub Actions test harness and its ordinary Actions runner use** for disposable/synthetic PG17 evidence only. It **does NOT approve the proposed third SQL migration, deploy/apply it to Supabase Cloud, merge PR68, access hosted data, buy services, change secrets/billing/settings or approve a private-manuscript pilot**. GitHub Actions may consume ordinary runner minutes; no account spending configuration change is authorized.

### Actual verified context

- Effective `main` = `021379856d07611752832b44bfe951d6ae36f0b2`, from owner-merged [PR76](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/76), merged-main [Actions39075424325](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/actions/runs/39075424325) SUCCESS. Re-fetch at task start.
- [PR68](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/68) = OPEN/DRAFT/unmerged, head `cbb379fa4a4eaa9f576f3abcce2c2258d22cc551`; the proposed migration `supabase/migrations/20261015171325_restrict_book_privileges.sql` has **NO owner migration-apply approval**.
- Prior [PG17 blocked evidence](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/issues/74#issuecomment-6243322555), branch `codex/vel-sec-001`, proves source hash capture but **0 SQL tests run** because local Docker engine hung.
- **Global Task/CP/EB ID collision:** blocked security branch and unrelated [PR77](https://github.com/Ben-001-sys/Vellistry/pull/77) independently assigned **0012** with different Git blobs. **Do not reuse/rename/overwrite already-committed CP0012 as though immutable history were absent**. Preserve both historical branches and record collision/supersession before new implementation. Allocate a truly unused Task/CP/EB number after scanning *main and all open and relevant historical refs*, not only main. Use a freshly pinned valid immutable pack from latest `main`, before editing a test harness.

### Bounded Codex scope — preferred implementation architecture

1. **Codex alone implements**. New isolated branch/worktree from actual `main`, a scoped and explicitly owner-authorized Task with allowlist for one manual-only `.github/workflows/VEL-SEC-001-*.yml` plus necessary safe test helper, Task/CP/EB and reports. Commit owner-task evidence and validate/commit immutable ContextPack **before** edits. Existing PR68 branch/read-only source is not rewritten or cherry-picked. ChatGPT coordinates/independently reviews, owner merges.
2. The canonical **ONE automatic** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and its six-job enforcement contract **MUST stay unchanged**. First check whether an existing, suitable manual-only workflow can perform this test without code changes. If not, prepare a **single `workflow_dispatch`-only evidence workflow**, with *no* `push`, `pull_request`, `schedule`, `pull_request_target`, elevated permissions, secrets or writes. Keep read-only `contents: read`, checkout with `persist-credentials: false`, reasonable timeout, actionlint. Clearly separate it from automatic enforcement CI. Any flow requiring modifying the CI invariant or policy must be stopped for separate owner approval.
3. **GitHub dispatch constraint:** GitHub requires a `workflow_dispatch` workflow file to be present on **default branch** to permit manual start. Therefore Codex should deliver a draft PR containing only the manual harness, validation and evidence plan; the owner explicitly reviews and merges **that harness PR first** (only after full applicable CI). Then owner manually triggers the workflow from GitHub Actions (or delegates the actual dispatch in Codex with separately authorized tool capability), selecting the pinned reviewed revision/ref. Do not claim cloud test PASS before actual run. See official GitHub documentation: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/manually-run-a-workflow
4. In the GitHub **hosted Ubuntu runner**, start a disposable `postgres:17` service using the supported job-container/service-container pattern (the present `privileges` CI job already uses this pattern). No desktop Docker daemon, no hosted Supabase connections, no owner secrets/keys. Record `SELECT version()`, exact image digest, runner OS, dependency versions, start health, teardown. Runner deletion/expiration is not a substitute for proving scoped fixture rollback/cleanup; record both.
5. Fetch/read *exact pinned source* from PR68 into **temporary runner storage**, not the source migration tree/merged branch. Assert the four original Git blob IDs and SHA-256 checksums:
   - `supabase/migrations/20261009000000_initial_author_books.sql`: Git blob `192a736d1a5d6ffc6f239c74ed61e7b8d2528b3b`
   - `supabase/migrations/20261009010000_restrict_accepted_manuscript_dml.sql`: `0670a60f1c2e299e9771b9af1c677d97712174d9`
   - **Unapproved proposed** `supabase/migrations/20261015171325_restrict_book_privileges.sql`: `230b1540bb5b8962fd2b797d4f8a467d3c035978`
   - `tests/book_privileges_regression.sql`: `5feac95772f93330b29150dbc135d766e7b0392e`
   Source commit `cbb379fa4a4eaa9f576f3abcce2c2258d22cc551` must be treated as **unmerged/test-only**. Refuse SHA drift, missing fixture, unpinned target, failed source hash or any attempt to connect to real Supabase.
6. Test **TWO fresh isolated disposable databases/PG17 clusters**:
   **BEFORE** original migrations #1–2 plus original fixture's `skip_hardening` should fail *specifically* on the expected dangerous books/TRUNCATE ACL (verify matching diagnostic; unrelated error is FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE). **AFTER** apply proposed migration #3 strictly to the second disposable database/cluster, then original regression should PASS 48 ACL cases and owner/cross-author RLS cases. Need explicit supplemental negative/positive probes not in the original fixture: real REFERENCES/foreign-key attempt, TRIGGER DDL denial, owner-author SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE where intended, cross-author operations, forged owner, PUBLIC/role inheritance and cleanup. Observe actual PostgreSQL SQLSTATE/error, not just metadata expectation. Distinguish fixture-injected artificial PUBLIC TRUNCATE/default grants from cloud **observed** rights: these tests are **synthetic proof of local proposed fix**, not evidence that actual cloud defaults currently match the synthetic fixture.
7. Report structured before/after matrix with command, exit code, exact source hash, PostgreSQL version, test coverage, cleanup logs, and `PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN`. Upload sanitized logs via GitHub artifacts; no tokens, connection strings, manuscripts. Add FACT/INTERPRETATION/PROPOSAL in ExecutionBundle and Issue74, link actual GH Actions run and job IDs. Independent ChatGPT exact-head code/log review then owner *separately* decides whether the **specific third migration** can advance to a later scoped hosted-dev dry run/approval gate.
8. **Negative control:** if a manual workflow cannot satisfy repo's compliance/owner scopes, GitHub dispatch capability, or Actions runner provisioning, report BLOCKED with precise evidence rather than adding an auto-workflow, loosening gate, faking owner approval or testing hosted Supabase.

**Completion checkpoint:** Test harness PR and CI verified/owner-merged, **real manually triggered hosted-runner PG17 evidence** with reproducible before failure / after result, independent review. Until these steps actually happen, **PG17 NOT_RUN, PR68 migration NOT APPROVED, hosted Supabase UNCHANGED**. This issue comment does not dispatch Codex or run GitHub Actions itself.
